desc:
In postfix (reverse Polish) notation every binary operator is written after its two operands, so 3 4 + means 3 + 4 and 3 4 + 5 * means (3 + 4) * 5. No brackets are needed.

An expression is given as an integer array tokens. The four values 100001, 100002, 100003 and 100004 are the operators +, -, * and /. Every other token is an operand (a number) with absolute value at most 100,000.

Return true if tokens is a complete, well-formed postfix expression: when the tokens are processed from left to right, every operator finds two finished values to work on, and after the last token exactly one value is left. Only the shape matters; the numbers themselves and division by zero are irrelevant.

Example: [3, 4, 100001, 5, 100003] is valid (it is (3 + 4) * 5). [3, 100001, 4] is not (the operator has only one value before it) and neither is [1, 2] (two values remain).
constraints: A token in 100001..100004 is an operator; every other token is an operand with -100,000 ≤ value ≤ 100,000
hints: Imagine evaluating the expression with a stack of values. What does an operand do to the stack, and what does an operator do?
You do not need the values. Only the number of finished values on the stack matters: an operand adds one, an operator removes two and adds one back.
Keep a single counter depth. Fail as soon as an operator is met while depth < 2. After the last token the expression is valid exactly when depth == 1.
editorial: Evaluating a postfix expression uses a stack: an operand is pushed, an operator pops two values and pushes one result. The expression is well formed exactly when this process never runs short of values and ends with a single value. Since the actual values do not matter, the stack can be replaced by its size.

Scan the tokens with a counter depth starting at 0. An operand makes depth += 1. An operator needs two values, so if depth < 2 return false; otherwise two values are replaced by one and depth -= 1. At the end return depth == 1 (0 can only happen for an empty input, 2 or more means unused operands are left over).
Each token is looked at once: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
